import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt' and 'intro.pathway'
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway'])

# Group the data by 'intro.pathway' and calculate the mean mrt for each group
grouped_data = invasion_success.groupby('intro.pathway')['mrt'].mean()

# Perform an ANOVA to test for significant differences in mrt across introduction pathways
anova_result = f_oneway(*[invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == pathway]['mrt'] for pathway in grouped_data.index])

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt', 'intro.pathway', and invasion success metrics
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway', 'number.of.invaded.plots', 'area.of.occupancy.10km', 'invaded.niche.breadth'])

# Fit a linear model to examine the interaction between 'intro.pathway' and 'mrt' on 'number.of.invaded.plots'
model = ols('number.of.invaded.plots ~ C(intro.pathway) * mrt', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

# Fit a linear model to examine the interaction between 'intro.pathway' and 'mrt' on 'area.of.occupancy.10km'
model = ols('area.of.occupancy.10km ~ C(intro.pathway) * mrt', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

# Fit a linear model to examine the interaction between 'intro.pathway' and 'mrt' on 'invaded.niche.breadth'
model = ols('invaded.niche.breadth ~ C(intro.pathway) * mrt', data=invasion_success).fit()
anova_table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
anova_table

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import f_oneway

# Load the invasion_success dataset
invasion_success = pd.read_csv('/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv')

# Filter out rows with missing values in 'mrt', 'intro.pathway', and invasion success metrics
invasion_success = invasion_success.dropna(subset=['mrt', 'intro.pathway', 'number.of.invaded.plots', 'area.of.occupancy.10km', 'invaded.niche.breadth'])

# Group the data by 'intro.pathway' and calculate the mean mrt for each group
grouped_data = invasion_success.groupby('intro.pathway')[['mrt', 'number.of.invaded.plots', 'area.of.occupancy.10km', 'invaded.niche.breadth']].mean()

# Perform an ANOVA to test for significant differences in mrt across introduction pathways
anova_result_mrt = f_oneway(*[invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == pathway]['mrt'] for pathway in grouped_data.index])

# Perform an ANOVA to test for significant differences in number of invaded plots across introduction pathways
anova_result_plots = f_oneway(*[invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == pathway]['number.of.invaded.plots'] for pathway in grouped_data.index])

# Perform an ANOVA to test for significant differences in area of occupancy across introduction pathways
anova_result_area = f_oneway(*[invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == pathway]['area.of.occupancy.10km'] for pathway in grouped_data.index])

# Perform an ANOVA to test for significant differences in invaded niche breadth across introduction pathways
anova_result_niche = f_oneway(*[invasion_success[invasion_success['intro.pathway'] == pathway]['invaded.niche.breadth'] for pathway in grouped_data.index])

grouped_data, anova_result_mrt, anova_result_plots, anova_result_area, anova_result_niche
